messages:
Jordan: Starting a heads-up — planning a short sunrise rollout tomorrow 04:30 UTC for az-eu-west1 GPU pools. Purpose: kernel microcode + graceful reboot to address rare driver OOMs we've seen on long-running jobs. Estimated per-rack impact ~10-12m, staggered across cohorts.
Maria: ETA on full fleet window?
Jordan: Total ops window 04:30-07:30 UTC. We'll do 6 cohorts, each cohort ~20 racks. Stagger 8m between cohorts, then 12m drain+reboot backfill.
Kevin: Which customers are on the affected racks? Any Dedicated pools pinned?
Jordan: Quick mapping: two Dedicated clusters (redwood-ded-3 and -7) overlap with cohort 2 and 4. We'll run nondisruptive migration for pinned tenants first, but need approval for short failover.
Ashley: Can we avoid APAC morning surge? 04:30 UTC is ~13:30 JST — mid-day. That's why I suggested sunrise instead of midnight. Is there an alternative?
Jordan: Good call. We picked 04:30 to hit EU low traffic while still before NA morning. APAC overlap is limited to a few edge tenants; team suggests targeted tenant comms + temporary capacity pair from az-apac1 to absorb spikes.
Maria: Ops checklist please — want prewarm KV cache and cold-start mitigations spelled out so LU/Tenant latency not regressed.
Jordan: Checklist (short):
- run `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on nodes in cohort
- prewarm cache via `scripts/kv-seed --cohort X --duration 2m`
- start canary pod in each rack before traffic shift
- monitor tail latency and token throughput in Console dashboard
- rollback window 3m after cohort completes

Kevin: Share the exact commands so oncall can run if needed.
Jordan: Commands snippet: ```bash
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-az-eu-01-rack-42
kubectl drain gpu-az-eu-01-rack-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=600s
# kv cache seed
./scripts/kv-seed --pool gpu-eu-01 --cohort 2 --rate 50
```

SRE-Bot: Scheduled maintenance ticket created: MNT-2026-0427-1023. Notifying affected tenants: redwood-ded-3, redwood-ded-7, gpu-edge-42.
Ashley: Cost question — if we spill to az-apac1 burst nodes, what's the unit cost delta? We need an estimate to decide whether to offer credits.
Jordan: Quick calc: baseline per-token serving cost in EU = $0.0008; APAC burst nodes use on-demand GPUs ~+30% => $0.00104. With expected spill of 5m tokens total during window, incremental cost ~ $1.2. Recommend simple goodwill credit to impacted tenants of $50 if SLA hit.
Kevin: Sounds reasonable. Also enable `fallback: model-compact` routing for non-Dedicated tenants to reduce token spend during drains.
Maria: Will ops attach a per-route SLO guard so Console can auto-revert rollout if 99th pct latency > 200ms for 5m?
Jordan: Yes — canary + auto-abort rule configured, I will push rollout policy: `abort-if(latency_99 > 200ms, 5m)` and `fallback-model=compact-v1` for best-effort traffic.
DevOps Bot: Canary deploy started for cohort 1 at 04:30 UTC simulated run. Logs: 0 drops, 1.2% latency delta.
Kevin: If the Dedicated clusters need manual migration, who owns the tenant comm? Product or Customer Success?
Jordan: I'll coordinate with CS — Maria, can you draft the tenant advisory? Include exact window, expected impact (soft failover), and the credit offer.
Maria: On it. Draft will go to #customer-success for review by EOD today.
Ashley: Last ask — please add a step to warm up embeddings cache too; we saw regressions last time when requests hit cold weights.
Jordan: Added to checklist: `embeddings-warmup --pool gpu-eu-01 --samples 1000`.
Kevin: Looks good. I'll be oncall during the window. If anything spikes, ping me @kevin. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Thanks all — will post final cohort schedule + CI job that generates per-rack mapping in ~2h.
